topic: Sepsis recognition and treatment on wards

audits.title: 711 A Clinical Audit of Adherence to Sepsis Protocol Initiation at Ward Level in a Level 3 (General Hospital)
audits.standard: HSE National Clinical Guideline no. 26 on sepsis protocol initiation (sepsis 6 bundle)
audits.setting: Two inpatient wards, Wexford General Hospital (level 3 general hospital)

cycle1.result: 36 (12.2%) positive sepsis triggers; HSE proforma used in 13.89% and completed in 1 case; average completion of sepsis 6 bundle 55.5%; antibiotics given in 31/36.

audits.other_findings: Revision of the sepsis proforma and further clinician education recommended.
audits.citation: Mehigan C, Kinsella U, Khan S, Coyle P. 711 A Clinical Audit of Adherence to Sepsis Protocol Initiation at Ward Level in a Level 3 (General Hospital). British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.269.

audits.title: The role of screening, SIRS and qSOFA in Head and Neck Sepsis: An Audit of 104 Patients

cycle1.result: Sepsis screening was poor; figures not reported.

audits.intervention: Suggested education and visual reminders such as posters or a clerking proforma.
audits.other_findings: Sepsis was very rare by qSOFA criteria; SIRS may overdiagnose sepsis.
audits.citation: Sheikh Z, Tan ET, Ifedayo S, Shahed QM. The role of screening, SIRS and qSOFA in Head and Neck Sepsis: An Audit of 104 Patients. . 2020. doi:10.22541/au.160555686.62186543/v1.

audits.title: An audit of ward nurses' knowledge of sepsis.
audits.standard: Standard sepsis definitions and Surviving Sepsis Campaign management guidelines
audits.setting: Medical, surgical and orthopaedic wards of one acute hospital (Chesterfield Royal Hospital)

cycle1.result: Some ward nurses appeared to have poor knowledge of the signs and symptoms of sepsis, severe sepsis/septic shock and some aspects of initial management (no figures in abstract).

audits.intervention: Educational initiatives introduced to raise awareness of sepsis definitions and Surviving Sepsis guidelines.
audits.other_findings: No re-audit reported after the education.
audits.citation: Robson W, Beavis S, Spittle N. An audit of ward nurses' knowledge of sepsis. Nurs Crit Care. 2007;12(2):86-92. doi:10.1111/j.1478-5153.2007.00210.x. PMID: 17883633.

audits.title: An audit of diagnosis and treatment of sepsis in north-central Nigeria.
audits.standard: Sepsis diagnostic criteria and standard sepsis management (appropriate empirical antibiotics within one hour, blood cultures)
audits.setting: Medical wards, Jos University Teaching Hospital

cycle1.result: 94/142 (66.2%) met sepsis criteria; 77 (82%) correctly classified for severity; empirical antibiotics inappropriate in 23 (24.5%) and none given within one hour; blood cultures available in 12.5%.

audits.other_findings: In-hospital mortality 53%; HIV/AIDS the commonest comorbidity (57.3%).
audits.citation: Isa SE, Iroezindu MO, Awang SK, Simji GS, Onyedibe KI, Mafuka, et al.. An audit of diagnosis and treatment of sepsis in north-central Nigeria. Niger J Med. 2013;22(4):319-325. PMID: 24283093.

audits.title: Improving Sepsis Management in the Acute Admissions Unit.
audits.standard: College of Emergency Medicine sepsis standards (e.g. high-flow oxygen 95%, crystalloid bolus 100%, lactate 95%, blood cultures 95%)
audits.setting: Acute admissions unit, Great Western Hospital

cycle1.result: High-flow oxygen documented 24%; crystalloid boluses 52%; lactate 66%; blood cultures 52%; only 3% received all six parts of the bundle.

audits.intervention: Sepsis proforma based on Sepsis Six; sepsis working group educating junior doctors and nurses with posters, pocket cards and teaching sessions.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in all parts of the Sepsis Six bundle and an 8% improvement in patients receiving all six.

audits.other_findings: Emergency department comparison figures: oxygen 100%, fluids 90%, lactate 93%, cultures 73%.
audits.citation: Adcroft L. Improving Sepsis Management in the Acute Admissions Unit. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2014;3(1):u204974.w2091. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u204974.w2091. PMID: 26734269.

audits.title: Improving management of severe sepsis and uptake of sepsis resuscitation bundle in an acute setting.
audits.standard: Best practice guidelines for severe sepsis resuscitation bundle (oxygen, IV fluids, antibiotics, blood cultures, lactate, urine output)
audits.setting: Acute medical unit, Worcestershire Royal Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Lactate measured 15/32 (47%); fluids within an hour 10/22 (45%); blood cultures taken after antibiotics 12/22 (55%); antibiotics within an hour 12/22 (55%).

audits.intervention: A set of interventions including a 'sepsis box'.

cycle2.result: Antibiotics within an hour up by 22%; lactate performed in 26/30 (87%); improved identification of severe sepsis and IV fluid administration.

audits.other_findings: A repeat over three months showed sustained improvement.
audits.citation: Kafle S, Nath N. Improving management of severe sepsis and uptake of sepsis resuscitation bundle in an acute setting. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2014;3(1):u204152.w1807. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u204152.w1807. PMID: 26734299.

audits.title: Improving multidisciplinary severe sepsis management using the Sepsis Six .
audits.standard: Sepsis Six protocol and national severe sepsis guidelines
audits.setting: Medical admissions, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford / Wexham Park Hospital

cycle1.result: 1% appropriately managed; 19% admitted to ITU (6% died); length of stay 10 days.

audits.intervention: Active promotion of teamwork to initiate the protocol; trust-wide updated protocols.

cycle2.result: 67% adhered to the protocol (p<0.0001); 7% admitted to ITU (no deaths); length of stay 7 days (p<0.0001).

audits.citation: Bhat A, Asghar M, Raulia G, Mandal AK. Improving multidisciplinary severe sepsis management using the Sepsis Six . Clin Med (Lond). 2016;16(6):503-505. doi:10.7861/clinmedicine.16-6-503. PMID: 27927811.

audits.title: Improving Compliance With the Sepsis Six Care Bundle in the Surgical Emergency Department: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: Sepsis Six bundle delivered within one hour of recognition
audits.setting: Surgical emergency department, Nishtar Hospital, Multan

cycle1.result: Bundle within one hour 15/60 (25.0%); median time to first antibiotic 95 minutes; sepsis documented 18/60 (30.0%).

audits.intervention: Educational sessions for medical and nursing staff, sepsis-awareness teaching and a standard sepsis proforma.

cycle2.result: Bundle within one hour 42/60 (70.0%); median time to antibiotic 50 minutes (p < 0.001); sepsis documented 51/60 (85.0%) (p < 0.0001).

audits.other_findings: All improvements remained significant after Holm-Bonferroni correction.
audits.citation: Ali B, Aizdee QH, Munir UA, Atif Kanjoo M, Mustafa FE. Improving Compliance With the Sepsis Six Care Bundle in the Surgical Emergency Department: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit. Cureus. 2026;18(8):e115139. doi:10.7759/cureus.115139. PMID: 42787907.
